chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who gathers women (concubines) whom he does not marry, if adultery occurs with them, the sin is upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping concubines or unmarried women for sexual relations in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the status of concubinage (milk al-yamin) by establishing that sexual relations with one's own concubines are not considered adultery (zina), but rather a distinct category where the sin of illicit intimacy falls upon the owner if he engages in it outside the bounds of ownership. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinguishes the legal status of concubines from free women, affirming that the master's right to sexual access does not constitute zina in the strict sense, yet carries its own moral and legal weight. The ruling underscores the continuity of pre-Islamic and Quranic practices within the Shia legal framework, emphasizing personal responsibility for the specific nature of the relationship.
